abstract.para: This topic covers installing the PCP packages.

topic.para: &productnameshort; ships PCP as regular packages in its base product repository, so no additional module or extension is required—only a registered system.
If you are not sure which mode a system is running, check VARIANT_ID in /etc/os-release: transactional means immutable, server means standard.
On the standard, non-immutable system, install the pcp package with &zypper;:

Alternatively, install the pcp-zeroconf package instead. It pulls in pcp as a dependency and additionally enables and starts pmcd, pmlogger, and pmproxy automatically, with a shorter, 10-second sampling interval. Use it if you want local monitoring running immediately without configuring the services yourself, as described in :
On the immutable mode of &productnameshort;, whose read-only root file system is only writable inside a new transactional snapshot, install either package through &tr-up; instead:

On the immutable mode, installing pcp also pulls in pcp-selinux, which is not part of the standard-mode dependency list. Changes take effect only after a reboot, since they live in a new snapshot until then:
